verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on five independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The kind 'missing-heading' is a misnomer. All five headings are present in the markdown with identical numbering and identical wording to the printed page: '## D.31.5.3 FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE function', '## D.31.5.4 SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT function', '## D.31.5.5 FORMATTED-DATE function', '## D.31.5.6 FORMATTED-TIME function', '## D.31.5.7 FORMATTED-DATETIME function' (page-1198.md lines 9, 16, 21, 26, 31). Each also carries an explicit anchor ( ... section-d-31-5-7). Not one word of heading text, and not one word of body text, is absent. The only thing that differs is the count of '#' characters. (2) THE CLAIM'S PREMISE ABOUT THE PDF IS FALSE AS STATED. It asserts the five headings are printed 'at the same rank as D.31.5.1', phrased as though D.31.5.1 held some distinct printed rank that D.31.5.3-.7 share and that the markdown fails to honour. Measured directly from the PDF text layer (PyMuPDF span metadata, doc indices 1195 and 1197 = printed pages 1196 and 1198): EVERY clause heading in this region is Cambria,Bold at 11.67 pt -- D.31.4 'Locale date and time intrinsic functions', D.31.4.1 'General', D.31.4.2 through D.31.4.5, D.31.5 'International date and time format handling', D.31.5.1 'General', and all of D.31.5.3 through D.31.5.7. A style census over pages 1190-1199 returns exactly two bold styles: 11.67 pt Cambria,Bold x42 (every heading) and 10.7 pt Cambria,Bold x3 (the three table column headers on page 1197). Left margins are 63.5 pt on page 1196 and 80.0 pt on page 1198, which is the mirrored verso/recto page margin, not an indentation rank -- within each page every heading shares one x0. The PDF therefore carries ZERO typographic rank information; hierarchy is conveyed solely by the clause NUMBER. The PDF supplies no evidence whatsoever that D.31.5.3 should sit deeper than, level with, or shallower than D.31.5.1 in the markdown, so there is no PDF fact for the markdown to contradict. (3) THE PATTERN IS A DOCUMENT-WIDE CONVERSION ARTIFACT, NOT A PAGE-1198 DEFECT. The '#' count in ISO_COBOL.md encodes no hierarchy anywhere in the 1261-page transcription. Census of every numbered heading in the file: depth-3 clauses render as '##' 337 times, '###' 532 times, '####' 19 times; depth-4 as '##' 241 / '###' 668 / '####' 32; depth-5 as '##' 144 / '###' 151 / '####' 43. The tool consistently gives the FIRST child of a parent one extra level and then flattens the remaining siblings back to '##' -- e.g. '### D.18.2.1 General' then '## D.18.2.2 Specification'; '#### 8.4.2.2.1 General' then '## 8.4.2.2.2 General format'; '### D.31.2.5' then '## D.31.2.6'; '### D.31.3.2' then '## D.31.3.3'. Even '## D.31.2' sits at the same markdown level as its own parent '## D.31'. The D.31.5.1-vs-D.31.5.3 delta on this page is one instance of an artifact occurring on the order of a thousand times; if anything the anomaly is the '###' on D.31.5.1, not the '##' on D.31.5.3. (4) THE STATED CONSEQUENCE DOES NOT FOLLOW. The page-1197 sentence 'described in D.31.5.3 through D.31.5.11' navigates by CLAUSE NUMBER. Those clause numbers are reproduced verbatim in the markdown headings and are additionally addressable via the generated anchors section-d-31-5-3 through section-d-31-5-11. No cross-reference in this document resolves through markdown outline nesting. The navigation promise is fully intact. (5) NO MEANING CHANGES. Independent line-by-line comparison of the rendered page against page-1198.md confirms the body text is faithful: the fractional-seconds decimal-separator/DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA paragraph with the 1-to-9 range; FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE returning '19950215T05142781-0500'; the CURRENT-DATE 'T' NOTE; SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT with 5:14:27.812479168304 -> 18867.812479168304; FORMATTED-DATE with the double-hyphen dashes, 'YYYYMMDD' and 143951 -> 19950215; FORMATTED-TIME with 'hhmmss.ss+hhmm', +300 and '05142781+0500'; FORMATTED-DATETIME's four arguments. The only other divergence is that the markdown's D.31.5.7 paragraph carries through the sentence the printed page cuts off at 'in the specified format. For' -- ordinary page-break reflow, explicitly a rejection criterion. This is formatting metadata invented by the converter, uniform across the whole document, with no counterpart in the source and no effect on content or navigation.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The five headings D.31.5.3 through D.31.5.7 are present in the markdown with their clause numbers and titles intact and individually anchored; nothing is missing. The PDF encodes no heading rank at all in this region -- D.31.4, D.31.4.1-.5, D.31.5, D.31.5.1 and D.31.5.3-.7 are all typeset identically as Cambria,Bold 11.67 pt at a single per-page left margin -- so the claim's appeal to a printed rank shared with D.31.5.1 has no basis in the source. The '##' versus '###' variation is a global artifact of the markdown conversion (depth-3 clauses appear as ## 337x / ### 532x / #### 19x across the file; the first child of each parent gets an extra level and later siblings flatten), and cross-references such as page 1197's 'D.31.5.3 through D.31.5.11' resolve by clause number, not by outline nesting. No content or meaning differs.
